messages:
lina_cs: Quick weekly check-in for account: Helix Media — focusing on Dedicated GPU usage and backpressure indicators. Posting the main metrics and a short ask.

lina_cs: TL;DR: GPU hours down 3% w/w, but saturation spike on 3/18 causing queue depth increases and some p95 latency regressions. Spend still within committed hours but queue tailing looks risky.

lina_cs: Metrics snapshot (24h window ending 1798123200):
- GPU hours used: 1,920h (commit 2,000h)
- Average pool saturation: 72% (peak 98% during 10:30-11:10 UTC)
- Queue depth (avg): 6; queue depth (peak): 42
- Inference p50/p95 latency: 62ms / 420ms (normal baseline ~55ms / 260ms)
- Error rate (5xx): 0.6% -> 1.8% during peak windows
- Spend against reserved: 96% of monthly commitment

lina_cs: Attachments: I ran the usual queries and a quick breakdown by tenant; main offender is helix-batch jobs that spiked concurrency.

derrick_sre: looking. can you share the query you used for queue depth?

lina_cs: sure — quick SQL we run in observability:```sql
SELECT
  ts_bucket(1m, ts) as minute,
  sum(active_jobs) as active_jobs,
  max(queue_depth) as max_q
FROM gpu_pool_metrics
WHERE pool = 'dedicated-helix'
AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

sophie_eng: I checked the model routing logs — at 10:25 UTC we retried ~8k small requests due to transient nvlink error on node gpu-17, and the router bumped more traffic to smaller instances, so batching reduced and p95 jumped.

mike_ops: node gpu-17 had a kernel OOM and restarted the runtime at 10:23. kube-autoscaler added 2 nodes but there was ~7m of cold-starts for some shards.

derrick_sre: ok that explains the saturation spike + queue tail. queue depth peak 42 matches backlog while shards rebalanced.

lina_cs: customer impact note: Helix's ingestion pipeline timed out on ~1.6% of requests during the 10:20-10:40 window; they logged support tickets. Renewal risk: small but worth proactive outreach.

sophie_eng: action items from infra side:
- patch runtime to reject on nvlink transient patterns (prevent retries) — PR ready (#442)
- add quicker shard warm-up so new nodes pick up warmed KV caches (work queued)

mike_ops: ops actions:
- increase min pool by +1 node during Helix peak windows (09:30-12:00 UTC) as a short-term mitigation
- add alert: queue_depth >= 25 for 5m -> page SRE oncall

derrick_sre: can we also add a cost check? If we bump min pool we'll burn extra reserved hours. need to calculate delta.

lina_cs: quick estimate: +1 node (v100) during 2.5h/day for 10 business days = ~62 additional GPU hours — still inside margin but lowers cushion. I'll confirm with billing.

capacity-bot: Automated note — reserved commit utilization updated: current utilization 97%. Projected daily burn rate with +1 node = +3.2% utilization over the month.

sophie_eng: proposed timeline: patch runtime -> deploy to dedicated canary tonight -> monitor for 48h. If stable, roll to all dedicated pools by EOW.

mike_ops: I'll enable temporary min-pool bump for Helix starting tomorrow 09:00 UTC and revert if we don't see repeat spikes.

lina_cs: I'll reach out to Helix AM with a short incident note + recommended plan and offer an enablement session on routing preferences and batch sizing.

derrick_sre: follow-ups:
- Sophie to merge runtime PR and coordinate canary (sophie -> @derrick_sre)
- Mike to add alert and enact min-pool bump (mike -> @lina_cs when done)
- Lina to share customer note and spend delta (lina -> Helix contact)

lina_cs: thanks — I'll update this thread when Helix AM replied or when ops changes are in. :thumbsup:

mike_ops: min-pool bump scheduled at 09:00 UTC tomorrow. will post status.

capacity-bot: Alert created: queue_depth_alert_helix (threshold: 25 for 5m).
